123	@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
124	+-- 141_reading_deferrals.sql
125	+-- SCHEMA migration (T-079, AT-17; no data). A reading can be deferred on the record, and every deferred act lists with
126	+-- its age from one view.
127	+--
128	+-- WHY. The owner (2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate "so long as it runs eventually"; nothing in the repository
129	+-- enforced or even measured it. A search not run and a source not mined each carried a deferral and a date; a source
130	+-- not read had no deferred state, so "chosen not to read yet" could not be told from "nobody has looked", and no query
131	+-- listed all of them with their age. What reaches the guidebook without it: a source whose full text is owed for a
132	+-- parameter, deferred once, never read, and indistinguishable from one deferred last week.
133	+--
134	+-- reading_deferrals is a table of its own. Rejected: a source_scans row (its file_sha256 and text_scope describe a
135	+-- reading that HAPPENED; a deferral is the opposite fact); evidence_sources.data_capture_status (one value per source,
136	+-- no date, no reason, and a column a data migration INSERTs); a new v_scan_ledger status (the pair stays owed until it
137	+-- is read, and every gate that reads the ledger's statuses would change meaning). A deferral is DISCHARGED BY
138	+-- DERIVATION, never by a write: the view below drops it when a full reading covers it.
139	+--
140	+-- v_deferred_acts is a cross-stage pointer view (CLAUDE.md section 3): it reads research (search_executions,
141	+-- citation_mining), evidence (evidence_sources, source_scans, reading_deferrals) and judgment (term_adjudications,
142	+-- observed_terms), plus base (base_parameters). Nothing reads it as a gate: what age makes a standing deferral a defect
143	+-- is the owner's to say, and no threshold is stored or typed anywhere. The age query is
144	+--   SELECT * FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE deferred_at < datetime('now', '-<N> days') ORDER BY deferred_at;
145	+
146	+CREATE TABLE reading_deferrals (
147	+    deferral_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
148	+    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
149	+    -- NULL: the whole-source catalogue reading is what is deferred.
150	+    parameter_id        INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
151	+    reason              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (trim(reason) <> ''),
152	+    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
153	+    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL
154	+);
155	+
156	+CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
157	+-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
158	+--   kind                subject
159	+--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
160	+--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
161	+--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
162	+--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
163	+-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
164	+-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none.
165	+-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
166	+-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. An older search row carries only a date; every other
167	+-- row, and any search logged now, a minute.
168	+--
169	+-- WHAT EACH ARM DROPS, and why (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
170	+--   search        NOTHING. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so every deferred
171	+--                 search lists, including one whose cell a later search has since covered. Not derivable today.
172	+--   mining        a row whose source's citation_mining_status is no longer 'deferred' (the owner's execution signal,
173	+--                 2026-09-18: db.py log-mining --discharge-deferral clears the row and the status together). A row whose
174	+--                 ref resolves to no evidence_sources row (a lead anchor) has no status to read and lists while its own
175	+--                 deferred_reason stands. created_at is the ROW's: a row first written by a pass that ran and deferred
176	+--                 later is dated from the pass.
177	+--   reading       a deferral whose source is now superseded (the replacement is what is owed) or whose parameter is no
178	+--                 longer active (the ledger drops it), and one a FULL reading dated at or after the deferral covers:
179	+--                 for a parameter, the strongest covering reading v_scan_ledger names is full-scope; for a NULL
180	+--                 parameter, any full catalogue reading. Dates are minute-resolution, so "at or after".
181	+--   adjudication  an observation whose LATEST adjudication (highest adjudication_id, the rule alias and rename writers
182	+--                 use) is not DEFERRED: a later judgment of any other outcome discharges it.
183	+SELECT 'search' AS kind,
184	+       'exec ' || se.exec_id || COALESCE(' ' || se.slug, '') AS subject,
185	+       se.mined_ref_id AS ref_id,
186	+       se.parameter_id AS parameter_id,
187	+       se.deferred_reason AS reason,
188	+       se.created_at AS deferred_at,
189	+       se.created_by_session AS created_by_session
190	+  FROM search_executions se
191	+ WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
192	+UNION ALL
193	+SELECT 'mining',
194	+       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) || ' ' || cm.slug,
195	+       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id),
196	+       NULL,
197	+       cm.deferred_reason,
198	+       cm.created_at,
199	+       cm.created_by_session
200	+  FROM citation_mining cm
201	+  LEFT JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id)
202	+ WHERE cm.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
203	+   AND (e.ref_id IS NULL OR e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred')
204	+UNION ALL
205	+SELECT 'reading',
206	+       d.ref_id || ' ' || COALESCE('parameter ' || d.parameter_id, 'whole source'),
207	+       d.ref_id,
208	+       d.parameter_id,
209	+       d.reason,
210	+       d.created_at,
211	+       d.created_by_session
212	+  FROM reading_deferrals d
213	+  JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = d.ref_id AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
214	+ WHERE (d.parameter_id IS NULL
215	+        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_parameters p
216	+                    WHERE p.parameter_id = d.parameter_id AND p.status = 'active'))
217	+   AND NOT EXISTS (
218	+         SELECT 1
219	+           FROM source_scans s
220	+          WHERE s.ref_id = d.ref_id AND s.text_scope = 'full' AND s.created_at >= d.created_at
221	+            AND CASE WHEN d.parameter_id IS NULL
222	+                     THEN s.mode = 'catalogue'
223	+                     ELSE s.scan_id = (SELECT l.scan_id FROM v_scan_ledger l
224	+                                        WHERE l.ref_id = d.ref_id AND l.parameter_id = d.parameter_id
225	+                                          AND l.text_scope = 'full') END)
226	+UNION ALL
227	+SELECT 'adjudication',
228	+       'observation ' || o.observation_id || ' ' || o.ref_id || ' ' || o.surface_form,
229	+       o.ref_id,
230	+       NULL,
231	+       a.rationale,
232	+       a.created_at,
233	+       a.created_by_session
234	+  FROM term_adjudications a
235	+  JOIN observed_terms o ON o.observation_id = a.observation_id
236	+ WHERE a.outcome = 'DEFERRED'
237	+   AND a.adjudication_id = (SELECT MAX(b.adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications b
238	+                             WHERE b.observation_id = a.observation_id);
239	+
240	+PRAGMA user_version = 141;

426	+    """Record that a READING of a source is owed and deliberately not done yet (migration 141, T-079, AT-17).
427	+
428	+    "Deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually" (owner, 2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate when it is on the
429	+    record with its date, so it can be listed and aged (`v_deferred_acts`). A pair no one has read is NOT-READ in
430	+    `v_scan_ledger` whether or not anyone decided to wait; this row says someone did, and why. THIS VERB WRITES
431	+    reading_deferrals AND NOTHING ELSE: the pair stays owed in the ledger, and the deferral is discharged by DERIVATION
432	+    when a full reading covers it (the view reads `v_scan_ledger`, never a flag a writer sets). `parameter_id` None
433	+    defers the whole-source catalogue reading.
434	+
435	+    REFUSES: a blank reason; an unknown or superseded source (the replacement is what is owed: `_refuse_tombstone`);
436	+    a parameter that does not exist or is not active; a pair a full reading already covers, or, for the whole source,
437	+    a source with no active parameter left without one (nothing is owed); a pair that already has a standing deferral
438	+    (asked of `v_deferred_acts`, the one definition of "standing"). A partial, fragment or abstract reading covers
439	+    nothing here, as in the ledger."""
440	+    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, "defer-reading",

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id
-----
CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,

    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)

CREATE TABLE "extraction_follow_ups" (
    follow_up_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    extraction_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    reason              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('read-outside-admitting-purpose', 'absence-needs-tested-value')),
    warrant             TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(warrant)) > 0),
    raised_at           TEXT    NOT NULL,
    raised_by_session   TEXT    NOT NULL,

    resolved_by_session TEXT,
    resolution          TEXT,
    CHECK ((resolved_at IS NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NULL AND resolution IS NULL)
        OR (resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NOT NULL
            AND resolution IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(resolution)) > 0))
)

CREATE TABLE term_adjudications (
    adjudication_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    observation_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    -- OUTCOMES, documented HERE and not inside the CHECK. dbcore.check_values() reads
    -- this constraint's own value list to build the CLI's refusal, and an inline
    -- comment between the quoted values defeats its parser -- measured 2026-09-03,
    -- when a first cut of this migration carried the descriptions inside the IN(...)
    -- and every legitimate outcome was refused with a mangled vocabulary. The whole
    -- reason vocabularies come from the schema rather than a list in the code
    -- (CLAUDE.md §4) is defeated by punctuation the parser cannot see past.
    --
    --   NAMES-EXISTING  names a term we already hold
    --   NAMES-NEW       names a concept new to the vocabulary
    --   NOT-OURS        a real phrase, but not one of our concepts
    --   DEFERRED        cannot be settled on this source alone
    outcome             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
                            ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')),
    term_id             TEXT REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    -- NOT NULL: an adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested, and the
    -- whole point of splitting observation from judgment is that the judgement is
    -- inspectable.
    rationale           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- The outcome and the pointer must agree. An outcome that names a term must name
    -- one; an outcome that declines must not.
    CHECK (
        (outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND term_id IS NOT NULL)
     OR (outcome IN ('NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')        AND term_id IS NULL)
    )
)

CREATE TABLE "citation_mining" (
    slug                TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),

    backward            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(backward IN (0,1)),

  exec_id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

     ('clinical','sr_meta','standard_eb','national_fw','code','co1','co2','grey')),

  -- depth as real method, not booleans:
  depth_method         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (depth_method IN ('scoping','systematic')),
  mining_direction     TEXT CHECK (mining_direction IS NULL OR mining_direction IN

  deferred_reason      TEXT,                 -- non-NULL => deliberate no-search for this cell

# is to carry a sentence. See dbcore.Refusal for why these are a subclass rather than plain
# ValueError -- in short, so that a defect keeps the traceback a refusal does not need.
from dbcore import Refusal                                         # noqa: E402


def _retrieval_log():
    """`scripts/research/retrieval_log`, imported on first use.

    It lives beside the bytes and outside the write path on purpose (its own docstring says
    why), and most verbs never need it, so it is not imported at module load.
    """
    research = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "research")
    if research not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, research)
    import retrieval_log                                              # noqa: E402
    return retrieval_log


def _ladder_evidence_types():
    """The evidence-type vocabulary, from the ratified ladder (CLAUDE.md rule 8).

    `schemas/tier_derivation.TIER_MAP`'s keys are the authority `add-source` already
    validates against. Used for argparse `choices=` where the column being written
    declares no CHECK of its own, so `dbcore.schema_choices()` has nothing to read.

    Returns None rather than raising if schemas is not importable: a parser that cannot
    be built is worse than one without a choices constraint, and the writer refuses the
    same values at run time either way.
    """
    try:
        from schemas.tier_derivation import TIER_MAP                 # noqa: E402
        return sorted({et for et, _ in TIER_MAP})
    except Exception:
        return None

# DB_PATH stays a module attribute because callers and tests read it. It is resolved
# through dbcore so there is one resolution, not two.
DB_PATH = dbcore.db_path()


# connect(), now(), audit(), _upd() and _validate_cols() MOVED to scripts/dbcore.py.
# They are re-exported here under their original names so that every existing caller
# and every skill that documents them keeps working unchanged (CLAUDE.md rule 4: a
# rename is not done until the callers are swept -- so this is not a rename).
connect = dbcore.connect
now = dbcore.now
audit = dbcore.audit
_upd = dbcore.upd
_validate_cols = dbcore.validate_cols


def _txn(conn, dry_run: bool = False):
    """`conn` itself when the caller already holds a write transaction, else a new one.

    Lets two writers share ONE transaction, so a refusal in the second rolls back the
    first. `add-source --slug` is the case: the source and its slug link are one
    admission. As two connect() blocks, a failure in the second left the first
    committed (GAP-058), and under --dry-run the link's foreign key could not see the
    rolled-back source, so the dry run crashed with a traceback instead of reporting.
    """
    return nullcontext(conn) if conn is not None else connect(dry_run)










def _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref_id: str, what: str):
    """Refuse to file new work against a SUPERSEDED source (a tombstone).

    supersede-source leaves the superseded row in place, and the determination engine
    gathers nothing from it (assess_cell.gather_sources: `superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL`).
    A writer that still accepted it filed an extraction, an observed term or a population
    grade that the engine then dropped without a word: work filed and lost. The same
    ground link-source-slug already refuses on, applied to the writers whose rows the
    engine would drop: add-extraction (and derive-extraction through it), observe-term,
    add-population-match.

    NOT ROUTED THROUGH HERE, on purpose:
      * log-search --admitted-ref-id, link-admission, resolve-candidate --admitted-ref-id:
        they record which search admitted which id, or what a candidate became -- history
        still true of the tombstone, and test_db_integrity S01 reads those edges.
      * log-mining, log-search --mined-ref-id: citation_mining_completeness does not
        filter superseded rows, so a tombstone may still owe a mining row or a deferral,
        and refusing would make that record unwritable.
      * add-economics-entry, raise-determination-gate: nothing drops them by the
        source's liveness; a row pointing at the tombstone is listed among its dependents
        by supersede-source.
      * amend-source, correct-source, amend-extraction, amend-population-match: they
        correct a row's own record, which stays legitimate after supersession.
    """
    row = conn.execute("SELECT superseded_by_ref_id FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?",
                       (ref_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is not None and (row[0] or "").strip():
        raise Refusal(
            f"{what}: {ref_id} is superseded by {row[0]}. A superseded source is a "
            f"tombstone: the determination engine gathers nothing from it "
            f"(assess_cell.gather_sources reads superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL), so work "
            f"filed against it is silently dropped. File it against {row[0]}. Nothing "
            f"was written.")


def _source_dependents(conn, ref_id: str) -> list:
    """Every row that points at source `ref_id`, by table and column, with its count.

    DERIVED from `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` over every table in sqlite_master, never a
    list: a table that gains a foreign key into evidence_sources is reported the day it
    exists. A column that points at a source WITHOUT a declared foreign key is not seen
    here; `superseded_by_ref_id` is the one such pointer on evidence_sources itself
    (test_db_integrity A09 stands in for its missing FK), so it is added by name.
    """
    out = []
    for (table,) in conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' ORDER BY name"):
        for fk in conn.execute('PRAGMA foreign_key_list("%s")' % table):
            # fk[2] is the parent table, fk[3] the child column, fk[4] the parent column
            # (None when the FK names the parent's primary key implicitly).
            if fk[2] != "evidence_sources" or fk[4] not in (None, "ref_id"):
                continue
            n = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s" WHERE "%s" = ?'
                             % (table, fk[3]), (ref_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            if n:
                out.append({"table": table, "column": fk[3], "rows": n})
    n = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_sources WHERE superseded_by_ref_id=?",
                     (ref_id,)).fetchone()[0]
    if n:
        out.append({"table": "evidence_sources", "column": "superseded_by_ref_id",
                    "rows": n})
    return out


def supersede_source(ref_id: str, by: str, reason: str, session: str,
                     dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Mark admitted source `ref_id` as SUPERSEDED BY admitted source `by` (GAP-060).

    The merge path for a source admitted twice: a mirror of an official document, or a
    DOI-less re-entry that test_db_integrity D04 reports as an author+year+title
    collision. Until this verb the only ways to merge were a curated exemption list
    (D04's KNOWN_DUP_SOURCE_KEYS, which leaves the mirror live and counted) or hand SQL.

    NEITHER ROW IS DELETED. `ref_id` keeps its id and every row that points at it, and
    gains `superseded_by_ref_id` plus a dated SUPERSEDED line in `notes`. Its dependents
    are REPORTED, not moved. Some readers skip a superseded source: assess_cell's gather
    (`superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL`), D04, link-source-slug, add-source's DOI duplicate
    check, and (since the review fix of 2026-10-01) add-extraction, observe-term and
    add-population-match, which refuse it rather than file work the engine drops. A figure
    extracted from the superseded row stops being gathered, so re-extract it from `by` if
    `by` does not already carry it.

    KNOWN GAP, NOT FIXED HERE. Views: v_item_provenance and v_source_reach_all skip a
    tombstone (migration 106_views_filter_retired). v_convergence_sources,
    v_determination_provenance, v_evidence_authors and v_source_admission still show one,
    each for a reason in that migration's header. Readers that are not views still list it too. Re-derive the views:
        select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%evidence_sources%'
           and sql not like '%superseded_by_ref_id%';

    Refuses: A == B; either missing; A already superseded; B itself superseded (no
    chains); a blank reason; and a LIVE determination resting on A
    (dbcore.determinations_resting_on) -- moving its source would change a written
    answer silently, so retire the specification first.

    Not refused, REPORTED: rows already superseded BY A. They appear in the dependents
    as evidence_sources.superseded_by_ref_id and, after this call, point at a tombstone.
    No verb re-points them; refusing would leave A's duplicate live with no way out.
    """
    a, b = dbcore.fold_ref(ref_id), dbcore.fold_ref(by)
    if not a or not b:
        raise Refusal("supersede-source needs both --ref-id and --by. Nothing was written.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"supersede {a}",
        why="A supersession that cannot say why cannot be contested.")
    if a == b:
        raise Refusal(f"{a} cannot supersede itself. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        rows = {r["ref_id"]: r for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT ref_id, superseded_by_ref_id, notes FROM evidence_sources "
            "WHERE ref_id IN (?, ?)", (a, b))}
        for rid, flag in ((a, "--ref-id"), (b, "--by")):
            if rid not in rows:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"{flag} {rid} is not in evidence_sources. Supersession is between "
                    f"two ADMITTED sources. Nothing was written.")
        if (rows[a]["superseded_by_ref_id"] or "").strip():
            raise Refusal(
                f"{a} is already superseded by {rows[a]['superseded_by_ref_id']}. A "
                f"supersession is not amended by a second call. Nothing was written.")
        if (rows[b]["superseded_by_ref_id"] or "").strip():
            raise Refusal(
                f"{b} is itself superseded by {rows[b]['superseded_by_ref_id']}. No "
                f"chains: supersede {a} by {rows[b]['superseded_by_ref_id']} instead. "
                f"Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_if_resting(
            conn, a, "Superseding it would change the evidence set of a written answer without "
                     "re-deciding it.", "supersede")
        dependents = _source_dependents(conn, a)
        stamp = now()
        notes = dbcore.append_dated_note(rows[a]["notes"], "SUPERSEDED", session,
                                         f"by {b}: {reason}", stamp)
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE evidence_sources SET superseded_by_ref_id=?, notes=?, updated_at=?, "
            "updated_by_session=? WHERE ref_id=?", (b, notes, stamp, session, a))

            SELECT ssl.local_ref_id, ssl.slug,
def _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, verb: str):
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT p.parameter_id, p.term_id, p.status, p.merged_into, p.notes, "
        "t.canonical_en FROM base_parameters p JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = p.term_id "
        "WHERE p.parameter_id = ?", (parameter_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise Refusal(f"{verb}: parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter.")
    return row


def _refuse_live_work(conn, parameter_id, verb: str):
    """Refuse while a LIVE determination or an OPEN determination gate stands on it.

    A retirement or a merge changes what the parameter IS. A live determination was
    computed on it and would silently become a determination of a folded or abandoned
    subject; an open gate is a question about it that nobody could then answer. Retired
    determinations and resolved gates are history and do not block.
    """
    live = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if live:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has LIVE determination(s) {live}. A "
            f"determination was computed on this parameter, and changing what the "
            f"parameter is would re-point it at a subject it was not computed for. Retire "
            f"each first (db.py retire-specification --specification-id N --reason ...), "
            f"then re-run this. Nothing was written.")
    gates = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT gate_id FROM determination_gates WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if gates:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has OPEN determination gate(s) {gates}. "
            f"Resolve each with its rationale first (db.py resolve-determination-gate "
            f"--gate-id N --rationale ...): an open gate is a question about this "
            f"parameter that nobody could answer once it is retired or merged. Nothing was "
            f"written.")


def _updated(conn, table: str, session: str, stamp: str) -> dict:
    """The updated_* columns this table actually has, set to one stamp."""
    have = set(dbcore.columns(conn, table))
    return {k: v for k, v in (("updated_at", stamp), ("updated_by_session", session))
            if k in have}


def retire_parameter(parameter_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire a parameter IN PLACE: status 'retired', the reason appended to its notes.

    Owner ruling 2026-09-16, "retire in place then": no row is deleted and the number is
    never reissued (base_parameters is AUTOINCREMENT, migration 076). The parameter's
    extractions, readings and history stay; every reader that lists or counts parameters
    filters on status (v_scan_ledger, v_value_independence since 104), and the writers
    already refuse an inactive parameter (add-extraction, raise-determination-gate,
    assess_cell's validate_parameter).

    REFUSES: a blank reason; a parameter that is not active (retired already, or merged
    -- its survivor is where work goes); a LIVE determination or an OPEN gate on it.
    """
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"parameter {parameter_id}",
        why="A retirement that cannot say why cannot be reviewed or reversed by decision.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "retire-parameter")
        if row["status"] != "active":
            target = f" into {row['merged_into']}" if row["merged_into"] else ""
            raise Refusal(
                f"retire-parameter: parameter {parameter_id} ({row['canonical_en']!r}) is "
                f"already {row['status']}{target}. Nothing was written.")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, parameter_id, "retire-parameter")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        notes = dbcore.append_dated_note(row["notes"], "RETIRED", session, reason, stamp)
        sets = {"status": "retired", "notes": notes}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [parameter_id])
        kept = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions "
                            "WHERE parameter_id = ?", (parameter_id,)).fetchone()[0]
        return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "canonical_en": row["canonical_en"],
                "status": "retired", "extractions_kept_as_history": kept,
                "dry_run": dry_run}


def merge_parameter(from_id: int, into_id: int, reason: str, session: str,
                    dry_run: bool = False):
    """Fold parameter `from_id` into `into_id`: two names for one quantity become one.

    Sets the folded row to status 'merged' with merged_into = the survivor -- the shape
    base_parameters' own CHECK has carried since 071 with no writer -- and RE-POINTS
    every row that holds the folded parameter_id at the survivor, with a dated MERGED
    line appended to each moved row's notes, in one transaction. The set of tables is
    READ FROM THE LIVE SCHEMA (every foreign key into base_parameters.parameter_id,
    including base_parameters.merged_into, so a chain of merges flattens onto the
    survivor); `_MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY` is the only exception list, each entry with its
    reason. A table that holds the id but has no notes column is refused rather than
    moved silently.

    REFUSES: the same id twice; a blank reason; either parameter not active; a LIVE
    determination or an OPEN gate on either. K02 then holds the survivor's next
    determination to every extraction it gained.
    """
    if from_id == into_id:
        raise Refusal("merge-parameter: --from and --into are the same parameter.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"merge {from_id} -> {into_id}",
        why="A merge that cannot say why two names are one quantity cannot be reviewed.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        a = _parameter_row(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        b = _parameter_row(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        for r, side in ((a, "--from"), (b, "--into")):
            if r["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(
                    f"merge-parameter {side}: parameter {r['parameter_id']} "
                    f"({r['canonical_en']!r}) is {r['status']}, not active. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        line = f"parameter_id {from_id} -> {into_id} (merge-parameter): {reason}"
        moved, kept = {}, {}
        tables = [t for (t,) in conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name")]
        for t in tables:
            for fk in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")').fetchall():
                if fk[2] != "base_parameters" or (fk[4] or "parameter_id") != "parameter_id":
                    continue
                col = fk[3]
                n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}" WHERE "{col}" = ?',
                                 (from_id,)).fetchone()[0]
                if not n:
                    continue
                if t in _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY:
                    kept[f"{t}.{col}"] = n
                    continue
                cols = dbcore.columns(conn, t)
                if "notes" not in cols:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"merge-parameter: {t}.{col} holds {n} row(s) for parameter "
                        f"{from_id} and the table has no notes column to record the move "
                        f"on. Moving them silently would leave no trace on the rows; add "
                        f"the table to _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY with its reason, or give it a "
                        f"notes column, in a tooling PR. Nothing was written.")
                info = conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")').fetchall()
                pk = [r[1] for r in sorted((r for r in info if r[5]), key=lambda r: r[5])]
                key = pk or ["rowid"]
                rows = conn.execute(
                    f'SELECT {", ".join(chr(34) + k + chr(34) for k in key)}, notes '
                    f'FROM "{t}" WHERE "{col}" = ?', (from_id,)).fetchall()
                for r in rows:
                    sets = {col: into_id,
                            "notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(r["notes"], "MERGED",
                                                              session, line, stamp)}
                    sets.update(_updated(conn, t, session, stamp))
                    try:
                        conn.execute(
                            f'UPDATE "{t}" SET ' + ", ".join(f'"{k}" = ?' for k in sets)
                            + " WHERE " + " AND ".join(f'"{k}" = ?' for k in key),
                            list(sets.values()) + [r[k] for k in key])
                    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                        raise Refusal(
                            f"merge-parameter: re-pointing {t}.{col} collided with a row "
                            f"the survivor already holds ({exc}). Resolve that row first. "
                            f"Nothing was written.") from exc
                moved[f"{t}.{col}"] = len(rows)
        notes = dbcore.append_dated_note(
            a["notes"], "MERGED", session,
            f"merged into parameter {into_id} ({b['canonical_en']!r}): {reason}", stamp)
        sets = {"status": "merged", "merged_into": into_id, "notes": notes}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [from_id])
        return {"from": from_id, "into": into_id, "from_name": a["canonical_en"],
                "into_name": b["canonical_en"], "re_pointed": moved,
                "kept_as_history": kept, "dry_run": dry_run}


def annotate_parameter(parameter_id: int, note: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Append a dated, attributed line to a parameter's notes. Never overwrites.

    The correction route a wrong note lacked (critique F18: parameter 12's note says "no
    source adjudication behind it" while TERM-091 carries a NAMES-NEW adjudication). Any
    status: correcting the record of a retired parameter is still a correction.
    """
    note = (note or "").strip()
    if not note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note is required and may not be blank.")
    if " || " in note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note contains ' || ', the separator every "
                      "dated line in notes begins with; it would make one annotation read "
                      "as two. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "annotate-parameter")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        sets = {"notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(row["notes"], "ANNOTATED", session,
                                                  note, stamp)}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""db.py's amendment writers from batch 20: every refusal proven to fire, and the
legitimate shape proven to pass.

WHY THIS EXISTS, as CLAUDE.md section 8 requires. db.py's Act-2 banner says "every refusal
here has a selftest case proving it fires AND a case proving the legitimate shape still
passes". Batch 20 (2026-09-25) added link-admission, amend-population-match, amend-term and
resolve-candidate --suggested-slug with no case at all, and a review that simply RAN them
found five defects no gate had seen:
  * link-admission refused a second admitting search, which log-search permits;
  * link-admission left results_admitted behind its own edges (exec 90 read 0 with 1 edge);
  * amend-term could never detect an unchanged scope_note, and nested each audit line
    inside the next;
  * --suggested-slug accepted a MERGED slug and a REHOME pointing at its own origin, and
    could not be required, so REHOME rows could still name no destination;
  * dbcore.fold_ref upper-cased the mixed-case Co1-NN namespace, so every writer that
    folds a ref id would have refused a genuine Co1 source.
What reaches the guidebook without these cases: a wrong provenance edge nothing can remove,
a coverage view that under-counts what searches yielded, a candidate "rehomed" nowhere, a
Co1 source that cannot be graded -- each looking fine to every gate.

Section D (migration 101, GAP-061's prerequisite) holds `decline-parameter` and the one
refusal it adds to `add-parameter` to the same standard. What reaches the guidebook
without it: a term judged NOT to be a design parameter minted as one anyway, so
extractions and determinations can key on a concept somebody already ruled out.

Section S (GAP-058) holds `add-source --slug` to "refuse before any write": a refused
admission used to leave its source and author rows committed, an orphan that is either
shipped or deleted by hand. It also holds `link-source-slug --local-ref-id`, the only way to

"""A fixture retrieval-log root that a pre-admission fetch cannot reach (T-073).

A batch persists what it fetched under the id its source will take BEFORE `db.py add-source` admits the source, so between
the two the retrieval log holds an id the database does not. A fixture that mints a source through the writer takes the
database's next id, which is that folder's id, and inherits the saved text: a refusal case then goes red for a reason that
has nothing to do with what it tests. The fix is to isolate the ROOT, not to change the id: a real admission must still take
the id its folder was filed under.

`fixture_log_root(dest, db_path)` symlinks into `dest` each folder of the repository's retrieval log EXCEPT a folder whose
manifest names a ref_id above the high-water mark of the database at `db_path`; such a folder is linked file by file with
only the lines and artefacts of those ids left out, and one line is printed for each.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sqlite3
import sys

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402


def fixture_log_root(dest, db_path, source=None):
    dest, source = pathlib.Path(dest), pathlib.Path(source or REPO / "retrieval-log")
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ro = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        high = dbcore.ref_id_high_water(ro)
    finally:
        ro.close()
    for d in sorted(source.iterdir()):
        if not d.is_dir():
            continue
        manifest = d / "manifest.jsonl"
        keep, ahead, stems = [], set(), set()
        if manifest.exists():
            for line in manifest.open(encoding="utf-8"):
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                rec = json.loads(line)
                ref = (rec.get("ref_id") or "").strip()
                m = dbcore._MINTABLE.fullmatch(ref)
                if m and int(m.group(1)) > high:
                    ahead.add(ref)
                    if rec.get("artefact"):
                        stems.add(pathlib.Path(rec["artefact"]).stem)
                else:
                    keep.append(line)
        if not ahead:
            link = dest / d.name
            if not link.exists():
                link.symlink_to(d.resolve())
            continue
        # A batch files several sources into one folder and admits them one at a time: leave out only the lines (and the
        # files) of the ids above the mark, not the artefacts of the sources already admitted (T-073 critic, 2026-11-15).
        print(f"fixture root: left out {sorted(ahead)} from {d.name} (above the copy's high-water mark {high})")
        out = dest / d.name
        out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (out / "manifest.jsonl").write_text("".join(keep), encoding="utf-8")

proposing an addition to `JurisdictionCode`.
ACTION: (1) Derive what is live before proposing a code, and name WHICH tables carry it — corpus or
reference. (2) Never write `GB`. (3) Do not admit a `lang_jur_map`-only code without a scope ruling.
(4) `TW` and `colloquial` are owed a decision.
DATE: 2026-09-18 — owner ruling, quoted above.

## Owner ruling 2026-09-18 — EXECUTED IS `mined`; a deferral is legitimate so long as it eventually runs

> **"executed is 'mined'"**
>
> and, immediately after:
>
> **"deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually"**

Given in answer to batch 16's finding that `citation_mining.backward` and `.forward` are set to `1`
by `log_mining` **unconditionally**, including on a deferral, so the direction flags do not
distinguish a pass that ran from one that was logged. Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0.

**WHAT IT SETTLES, AND IT NARROWS THE DEFECT RATHER THAN WIDENING IT.**

1. **The execution signal already exists and it is `evidence_sources.citation_mining_status`.**
   `mined` means the pass ran; `deferred` means it did not. The column is live, it is populated, and
   `log_mining` already derives it correctly (`deferred` with a reason, `mined` otherwise). Nothing
   new needs building to answer "did this source get mined".
2. **The direction columns are therefore not the home of that fact and must not be made one.**
   Batch 16's proposed remedy — split `backward`/`forward` into attempted-versus-executed pairs —
   is **refused by this ruling**: it would put one fact in a second home, which is rule 5, and the
   first home already answers it. `backward=1` says a backward pass was *logged*; the status says
   whether it *ran*. Read both.
3. **A deferral is not a defect.** Depth-1 is a hard constraint (`citation-miner` §6) and a batch
   that admits an anchor cannot mine it in the same pass. Deferring is the designed behaviour, and
   batch 16's three new deferrals are correct.

**WHAT REMAINS OWED, WHICH IS THE HALF THE RULING'S SECOND CLAUSE CREATES.** *"So long as it runs
eventually"* is an obligation, and **nothing in this repository enforces it or even measures it**.
There is no ageing on a deferred mining row, no backlog count, and no check that fails when a
deferral goes unhonoured. A deferral that is never discharged is indistinguishable from one taken
last week, and the register currently holds deferrals from batch 08 alongside batch 16's.

**AND ONE READING IS NOW WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY IMPRECISE.**
`citation_mining_completeness` counts **row presence**, so it reports deferrals as mined — measured
2026-09-18 at `10/10 T1-2 sources mined, 100.0%` repo-wide while the number of sources on
`accessible-circulation-geometry` whose backward pass had actually been executed was **3 of 13**.
Under this ruling that check is reading the wrong column: it must read `citation_mining_status`.
Derive both figures, never quote these:

**The snippet below derives BOTH quoted figures and nothing else.** The first version of it
derived neither — it printed a repo-wide tally across all tiers, so a reader told to re-derive
rather than trust got numbers that did not match the sentence above them. That is rule 7a's own
failure mode reappearing inside the remedy for it, and it is corrected here rather than excused.

4402:1. **The scan contract.** Every admitted source is read against the whole parameter list, whatever slug it was filed under. Slugs plan and log searches; they do not decide what is taken from a source. One source can yield many parameters. Arguments and qualitative findings are mined as well as

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py -- build the owner's browser page.

WHAT THIS IS. One HTML file that opens the guidebook database inside the viewer (sql.js, WebAssembly), so the
owner can read every table, follow every pointer and see what is waiting on them, from a phone. The request and
the owner's answer on the code it adds: references/project-standards.md, "Owner statement 2026-10-28".

WHAT IT INJECTS. The page derives tables, columns, keys, pointers and views from the embedded database. It cannot
derive four things, each read from its single home: the stage of a table (governance/stage-map.yaml), the
vocabularies and CHECK shapes (dbcore.check_values / check_expression), the determinations a source holds up
(dbcore.determinations_resting_on), and the glossary and queue (governance/owner-browser.yaml).

THE OUTPUT IS NEVER COMMITTED. --out inside the repository is refused: a rendered page is not a pipeline object
(workplan T-5, the report's K-13) and the repository's scratchpad/ is committed by rule 6. Publish the file as a
private Artifact. The output is a pure function of the database, the commit and the two YAML files.

USAGE
  python3 scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py --out /tmp/owner-browser/index.html [--db PATH] [--wasm PATH]
  --db defaults to GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, else the canonical file (opened read-only). --wasm skips the download.
Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 refused or misconfigured.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request

import yaml

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402

SQLJS_URL = "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/sql.js/1.10.3/"
SQLJS_WASM_SHA256 = "d7e61b828523001f26ce0b3f88dabcf6c12e5e6edf80eb4f08b26ac7b946ff88"

111:    ap.add_argument("--wasm")

## Verdict

The claim does not hold. On a scratch copy I produced four things it rules out: a live deferral the view drops, a discharged deferral the view lists forever (two routes), a pair deferred twice with neither row listed, and a test that goes red on ordinary corpus drift.

What held: the migration reproduces, capture and replay work, `build_graph --check` is unchanged, and the two task-listed mutations are killed.

I do not propose repairs; that is outside this role. Each finding gives the failing command and its output. Line numbers are at 25a07958; test-file lines are approximate.

All experiments ran on copies under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/82388ac1-2e44-55eb-8ade-e982067adc5f/scratchpad/antagonist-t079/`. The harness is `h.py`, experiments are `e1.py`–`e6.py`, mutations are `mut2.py` with results in `mut2.out`; my e1–e6 printouts were not saved to files, so re-run to reproduce. They import from a worktree at `/tmp/claude-0/antag79`, so re-add it to re-run. Both worktrees are removed. Canonical `data/guidebook.db` sha256 is unchanged (`b3f6997a…`), and the main tree is untouched.

## Findings, worst first

**F1 (HIGH). A mining pass under another slug hides a standing mining deferral.**
- Where: `scripts/migrations/141_reading_deferrals.sql:80` (`e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred'`).
- Claim broken: "a deferral is discharged when the act is done; nothing is dropped." T079-04 asserts a pass without `--discharge-deferral` leaves the deferral listed, but only tests the same slug.
- Failure case (`e3.py`): REF-00999 is deferred under `accessible-circulation-geometry` and also linked to `accessible-design-failures-poor-performance`. I ran `db.log_mining('accessible-design-failures-poor-performance','REF-00999','backward',S,notes=…)` with no discharge flag.
- Output: `{'logged': True, 'status_set': 'mined'}`. The original row's `deferred_reason` is still set, and `view('mining','REF-00999')` returns `[]`.
- The reply carries no `deferral_still_standing`. The commit message discloses the one-flag ambiguity but not that ordinary verbs reach it; no live row is in this state yet (0).

**F2 (HIGH). A whole-source deferral lists forever once every pair is covered by targeted full readings.**
- Where: migration `:99` (`THEN s.mode = 'catalogue'`) against `scripts/db.py:8659-8664`, the verb's "owed" test.
- Claim broken: "the one definition of standing". The verb and the view use two different coverage predicates.
- Failure case (`e1.py`): `defer(R, None)`, then `scan(R,'full','targeted',p)` for all 10 active parameters.
- Output: ledger non-full pairs `0`; the view still lists `REF-01037 whole source`; a second `defer(R, None)` is refused with "a full reading already covers REF-01037 for every active parameter, so no reading is owed".
- No writer can ever clear the row. T079-10 (about line 2782) asserts this behaviour as correct.
- Two sentences are false for this case: the owner-browser gloss "A full reading ends it" (`governance/owner-browser.yaml:71`) and the skill's "a `full` reading that covers it ends it" (`skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:145`).

**F3 (HIGH). The "at or after" tie hides a live whole-source deferral, and a duplicate is then accepted.**
- Where: migration `:97` (`s.created_at >= d.created_at`) combined with `:99`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`, all in one minute): full catalogue scan (catalogue_version 12); parameter 13 created (hand SQL, standing in for `add-parameter`); `defer(R2, None)`.
- Output: the deferral is accepted (`deferral_id 1`, `2026-11-16 21:05`), the ledger says `(R2,13)` is `NOT-READ`, and `view('reading',R2)` is `[]`.
- A second `defer(R2, None)` is also accepted (`deferral_id 2`). Two rows now exist, neither will ever list, and the standing refusal is bypassed.
- The tests pin `>=`: mutation M16 (strict `>` on the whole-source arm) turns T079-10 and T079-11 red.

**F4 (MEDIUM). `merge-parameter` creates an immortal deferral on the survivor.**
- Where: `scripts/db.py:7608` (re-points `source_scans.target_parameter_id`) against migration `:97`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`): a full targeted reading of `(R4, 4)` dated before a deferral of `(R4, 5)`; then merge 4 into 5.
- Output: ledger `(R4,5)` reads `READ-NOTHING-FOUND, full, scan 20`; the view still lists `REF-01039 parameter 5`; `defer-reading` says "a full reading already covers REF-01039 for parameter 5".
- The re-pointed scan predates the deferral, so the date clause never lets it discharge.

**F5 (MEDIUM). T079-01 goes red on corpus drift with no code change.**
- Where: `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py` about line 2700 (`aged.get("mining") == kinds.get("mining")`, `aged.get("search") == live_search`).
- Failure case (`mut2.py` D-DATA): unmutated code, one live mining deferral re-dated to now.
- Output: `RESULTS: 240/241 … RED: ['T079-01']`.
- The next batch that defers mining or a search will turn this red for 24 hours, then green by itself.
- The check is `advisory` in the registry, so none of T079-01…20 blocks anything.

**F6 (MEDIUM). Five mutations survive all 20 cases (241/241 each).**
- M3: mining arm dated by `updated_at`. This is the clock-reset failure task section 4 item 3 names.
- M4: search arm dated by `COALESCE(updated_at, created_at)`. Same failure.
- M8: the standing check without `kind = 'reading'`. A mining deferral on a source would then refuse its whole-source reading deferral.
- M15: the CLI drops `dry_run=args.dry_run`, so `--dry-run` writes. The commit lists this path as not verified.
- M17: no `fold_ref`.
- The two task-listed mutations are killed: M1 by T079-03/10/11/12, M2 by T079-05/14/18.

**F7 (MEDIUM). Merge and supersede both lose the deferral's age and reason for the pair that is now owed.**
- Merge (disclosed in the commit): the folded pair's row leaves the view and the survivor pair reads `NOT-READ` with no deferral.
- Supersede (not disclosed as a loss): after `supersede_source(R6,R7,…)`, `view('reading',R6)` and `view('reading',R7)` are both `[]`.
- Age is the only thing AT-17 asks for, so "nothing dropped" fails here.

**F8 (LOW-MEDIUM). `defer-reading` accepts a BLOCKED source.**
- Where: `scripts/db.py:8659`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`): a source with `processing_blocked_reason='paywalled'` has all 11 pairs `BLOCKED`; `defer(R3,PA)` and `defer(R3,None)` are both accepted and listed.
- The skill sentence (`skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:143-145`) scopes the verb to "the text obtainable" and says "the pair stays owed in the ledger"; the ledger calls a BLOCKED pair "not reading debt".
- It also accepts an `EXTRACTED` pair with no full reading (REF-00983, parameter 3).

**F9 (LOW). Five of seven refusals name no next action, a day after T-043 merged (c33b4936).**
- Checked against T-043's own cue regex.
- The five: `'REF-99999' is not an admitted source.`; `parameter_id 9999: no such parameter.`; `parameter N is retired…`; `a full reading already covers…`; `already has a standing deferral…`.
- The first two also omit "Nothing was written."

**F10 (LOW). Input gaps on the verb.**
- `--session " "` is accepted and stored as `' '`.
- `--reason $' ​'` is accepted as a one-character invisible reason; both Python `strip` and the SQL `trim` CHECK pass it.
- A 20,048-character reason with an embedded newline and ` || ` is accepted.
- There is no uniqueness in the schema. A two-process race did not reproduce (one of the two was refused), but F3 shows duplicates are reachable.

**F11 (LOW). The migration header misstates a stage.**
- `141_reading_deferrals.sql:17-18` puts `observed_terms` under judgment; `governance/stage-map.yaml:120` says `evidence`.

**F12 (LOW, unproven). Another deferred-act home is outside the view.**
- `gap_mining.outcome = 'deferred'` is not an arm. It holds 0 rows today, so this is unproven rather than clean.

**For the owner (doctrine).** The quoted 2026-09-18 ruling (`references/project-standards.md:3731-3737`) is about citation mining. Extending a legitimate deferred state to readings rests on the task author's "by extension", against the scan contract at `:4402` ("Every admitted source is read against the whole parameter list"). `grep -rn -i -E "defer.{0,30}reading|reading.{0,30}deferr" sessions/ decisions/ governance/*.md` returns nothing, so I found no ruling either way.

## What held

- **Migration:** `migrate_db.py --rebuild` exits 0; `sqlite_master` is equal (207 = 207), `user_version` 141 both, no table count differs; `migration_reproducibility.py --deep` PASS; integrity and foreign-key checks clean.
- **Rule 5:** `reading_deferrals` duplicates neither `source_scans` (readings that happened) nor `extraction_follow_ups` (per-extraction, two-value reason). `[NULL: second-home question — examined, nothing found]`
- **Capture and replay:** `emit_batch_sql` captured both deferral rows and they replayed identically onto a canonical copy, with the view listing them.
- **CLI:** `--dry-run` writes nothing; a `.md` session is stemmed; a lower-case ref is folded; blank, space, tab and newline reasons are refused; superseded, unknown-source, unknown-parameter and covered-pair refusals fire. No merged or retired parameter exists live, so the merged case was not run through the CLI.
- **Retire:** `retire-parameter` takes the deferral out of the view as stated.
- **Supersede is not blocked:** it reports `reading_deferrals` among dependents and proceeds.
- **Double counting:** no duplicate subjects in the live view; a deferred search and a reading deferral for the same cell list as two kinds, once each. One search deferred twice lists twice (execs 204 and 205), which the task chose.
- **Work-list usefulness:** live view is adjudication 22, mining 13, search 1, aged 10–89 days, 26 older than 30 days. It is not dominated by stale searches. The one search (exec 9, 2026-08-19) is a "wrong slug" deferral that will list permanently. `[NULL: dominance by covered searches — examined, nothing found]`
- **Adjudication arm:** it agrees with the batch-done read 3 rule (max `adjudication_id`); none of its rows sits on a superseded source. The predicate is a second copy in `.claude/commands/batch-done.md:98`, not a shared one.
- **Cost:** 580 hand-seeded deferrals read through the view in under 0.01 s. There is no index on `reading_deferrals`, and none is needed at this size.
- **`build_graph.py --check`:** parent 103 failures / 5 warnings, commit 103 / 5, FAIL and WARN lines identical.
- **`context_map.py --check`:** fresh.
- **Test file:** 241/241, EXAMINED 241, all 20 T079 ids present.
- **Not run:** the `owner_browser_build` render (needs a wasm download); `scan_debt` and `research_dod`, both untouched by the diff.

## Verdict

The claim does not hold. On a scratch copy I produced four things it rules out: a live deferral the view drops, a discharged deferral the view lists forever (two routes), a pair deferred twice with neither row listed, and a test that goes red on ordinary corpus drift.

What held: the migration reproduces, capture and replay work, `build_graph --check` is unchanged, and the two task-listed mutations are killed.

I do not propose repairs; that is outside this role. Each finding gives the failing command and its output. Line numbers are at 25a07958; test-file lines are approximate.

All experiments ran on copies under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/82388ac1-2e44-55eb-8ade-e982067adc5f/scratchpad/antagonist-t079/`. The harness is `h.py`, experiments are `e1.py`–`e6.py`, mutations are `mut2.py` with results in `mut2.out`; my e1–e6 printouts were not saved to files, so re-run to reproduce. They import from a worktree at `/tmp/claude-0/antag79`, so re-add it to re-run. Both worktrees are removed. Canonical `data/guidebook.db` sha256 is unchanged (`b3f6997a…`), and the main tree is untouched.

## Findings, worst first

**F1 (HIGH). A mining pass under another slug hides a standing mining deferral.**
- Where: `scripts/migrations/141_reading_deferrals.sql:80` (`e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred'`).
- Claim broken: "a deferral is discharged when the act is done; nothing is dropped." T079-04 asserts a pass without `--discharge-deferral` leaves the deferral listed, but only tests the same slug.
- Failure case (`e3.py`): REF-00999 is deferred under `accessible-circulation-geometry` and also linked to `accessible-design-failures-poor-performance`. I ran `db.log_mining('accessible-design-failures-poor-performance','REF-00999','backward',S,notes=…)` with no discharge flag.
- Output: `{'logged': True, 'status_set': 'mined'}`. The original row's `deferred_reason` is still set, and `view('mining','REF-00999')` returns `[]`.
- The reply carries no `deferral_still_standing`. The commit message discloses the one-flag ambiguity but not that ordinary verbs reach it; no live row is in this state yet (0).

**F2 (HIGH). A whole-source deferral lists forever once every pair is covered by targeted full readings.**
- Where: migration `:99` (`THEN s.mode = 'catalogue'`) against `scripts/db.py:8659-8664`, the verb's "owed" test.
- Claim broken: "the one definition of standing". The verb and the view use two different coverage predicates.
- Failure case (`e1.py`): `defer(R, None)`, then `scan(R,'full','targeted',p)` for all 10 active parameters.
- Output: ledger non-full pairs `0`; the view still lists `REF-01037 whole source`; a second `defer(R, None)` is refused with "a full reading already covers REF-01037 for every active parameter, so no reading is owed".
- No writer can ever clear the row. T079-10 (about line 2782) asserts this behaviour as correct.
- Two sentences are false for this case: the owner-browser gloss "A full reading ends it" (`governance/owner-browser.yaml:71`) and the skill's "a `full` reading that covers it ends it" (`skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:145`).

**F3 (HIGH). The "at or after" tie hides a live whole-source deferral, and a duplicate is then accepted.**
- Where: migration `:97` (`s.created_at >= d.created_at`) combined with `:99`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`, all in one minute): full catalogue scan (catalogue_version 12); parameter 13 created (hand SQL, standing in for `add-parameter`); `defer(R2, None)`.
- Output: the deferral is accepted (`deferral_id 1`, `2026-11-16 21:05`), the ledger says `(R2,13)` is `NOT-READ`, and `view('reading',R2)` is `[]`.
- A second `defer(R2, None)` is also accepted (`deferral_id 2`). Two rows now exist, neither will ever list, and the standing refusal is bypassed.
- The tests pin `>=`: mutation M16 (strict `>` on the whole-source arm) turns T079-10 and T079-11 red.

**F4 (MEDIUM). `merge-parameter` creates an immortal deferral on the survivor.**
- Where: `scripts/db.py:7608` (re-points `source_scans.target_parameter_id`) against migration `:97`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`): a full targeted reading of `(R4, 4)` dated before a deferral of `(R4, 5)`; then merge 4 into 5.
- Output: ledger `(R4,5)` reads `READ-NOTHING-FOUND, full, scan 20`; the view still lists `REF-01039 parameter 5`; `defer-reading` says "a full reading already covers REF-01039 for parameter 5".
- The re-pointed scan predates the deferral, so the date clause never lets it discharge.

**F5 (MEDIUM). T079-01 goes red on corpus drift with no code change.**
- Where: `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py` about line 2700 (`aged.get("mining") == kinds.get("mining")`, `aged.get("search") == live_search`).
- Failure case (`mut2.py` D-DATA): unmutated code, one live mining deferral re-dated to now.
- Output: `RESULTS: 240/241 … RED: ['T079-01']`.
- The next batch that defers mining or a search will turn this red for 24 hours, then green by itself.
- The check is `advisory` in the registry, so none of T079-01…20 blocks anything.

**F6 (MEDIUM). Five mutations survive all 20 cases (241/241 each).**
- M3: mining arm dated by `updated_at`. This is the clock-reset failure task section 4 item 3 names.
- M4: search arm dated by `COALESCE(updated_at, created_at)`. Same failure.
- M8: the standing check without `kind = 'reading'`. A mining deferral on a source would then refuse its whole-source reading deferral.
- M15: the CLI drops `dry_run=args.dry_run`, so `--dry-run` writes. The commit lists this path as not verified.
- M17: no `fold_ref`.
- The two task-listed mutations are killed: M1 by T079-03/10/11/12, M2 by T079-05/14/18.

**F7 (MEDIUM). Merge and supersede both lose the deferral's age and reason for the pair that is now owed.**
- Merge (disclosed in the commit): the folded pair's row leaves the view and the survivor pair reads `NOT-READ` with no deferral.
- Supersede (not disclosed as a loss): after `supersede_source(R6,R7,…)`, `view('reading',R6)` and `view('reading',R7)` are both `[]`.
- Age is the only thing AT-17 asks for, so "nothing dropped" fails here.

**F8 (LOW-MEDIUM). `defer-reading` accepts a BLOCKED source.**
- Where: `scripts/db.py:8659`.
- Failure case (`e2.py`): a source with `processing_blocked_reason='paywalled'` has all 11 pairs `BLOCKED`; `defer(R3,PA)` and `defer(R3,None)` are both accepted and listed.
- The skill sentence (`skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:143-145`) scopes the verb to "the text obtainable" and says "the pair stays owed in the ledger"; the ledger calls a BLOCKED pair "not reading debt".
- It also accepts an `EXTRACTED` pair with no full reading (REF-00983, parameter 3).

**F9 (LOW). Five of seven refusals name no next action, a day after T-043 merged (c33b4936).**
- Checked against T-043's own cue regex.
- The five: `'REF-99999' is not an admitted source.`; `parameter_id 9999: no such parameter.`; `parameter N is retired…`; `a full reading already covers…`; `already has a standing deferral…`.
- The first two also omit "Nothing was written."

**F10 (LOW). Input gaps on the verb.**
- `--session " "` is accepted and stored as `' '`.
- `--reason $'\u00a0\u200b'` is accepted as a one-character invisible reason; both Python `strip` and the SQL `trim` CHECK pass it.
- A 20,048-character reason with an embedded newline and ` || ` is accepted.
- There is no uniqueness in the schema. A two-process race did not reproduce (one of the two was refused), but F3 shows duplicates are reachable.

**F11 (LOW). The migration header misstates a stage.**
- `141_reading_deferrals.sql:17-18` puts `observed_terms` under judgment; `governance/stage-map.yaml:120` says `evidence`.

**F12 (LOW, unproven). Another deferred-act home is outside the view.**
- `gap_mining.outcome = 'deferred'` is not an arm. It holds 0 rows today, so this is unproven rather than clean.

**For the owner (doctrine).** The quoted 2026-09-18 ruling (`references/project-standards.md:3731-3737`) is about citation mining. Extending a legitimate deferred state to readings rests on the task author's "by extension", against the scan contract at `:4402` ("Every admitted source is read against the whole parameter list"). `grep -rn -i -E "defer.{0,30}reading|reading.{0,30}deferr" sessions/ decisions/ governance/*.md` returns nothing, so I found no ruling either way.

## What held

- **Migration:** `migrate_db.py --rebuild` exits 0; `sqlite_master` is equal (207 = 207), `user_version` 141 both, no table count differs; `migration_reproducibility.py --deep` PASS; integrity and foreign-key checks clean.
- **Rule 5:** `reading_deferrals` duplicates neither `source_scans` (readings that happened) nor `extraction_follow_ups` (per-extraction, two-value reason). `[NULL: second-home question — examined, nothing found]`
- **Capture and replay:** `emit_batch_sql` captured both deferral rows and they replayed identically onto a canonical copy, with the view listing them.
- **CLI:** `--dry-run` writes nothing; a `.md` session is stemmed; a lower-case ref is folded; blank, space, tab and newline reasons are refused; superseded, unknown-source, unknown-parameter and covered-pair refusals fire. No merged or retired parameter exists live, so the merged case was not run through the CLI.
- **Retire:** `retire-parameter` takes the deferral out of the view as stated.
- **Supersede is not blocked:** it reports `reading_deferrals` among dependents and proceeds.
- **Double counting:** no duplicate subjects in the live view; a deferred search and a reading deferral for the same cell list as two kinds, once each. One search deferred twice lists twice (execs 204 and 205), which the task chose.
- **Work-list usefulness:** live view is adjudication 22, mining 13, search 1, aged 10–89 days, 26 older than 30 days. It is not dominated by stale searches. The one search (exec 9, 2026-08-19) is a "wrong slug" deferral that will list permanently. `[NULL: dominance by covered searches — examined, nothing found]`
- **Adjudication arm:** it agrees with the batch-done read 3 rule (max `adjudication_id`); none of its rows sits on a superseded source. The predicate is a second copy in `.claude/commands/batch-done.md:98`, not a shared one.
- **Cost:** 580 hand-seeded deferrals read through the view in under 0.01 s. There is no index on `reading_deferrals`, and none is needed at this size.
- **`build_graph.py --check`:** parent 103 failures / 5 warnings, commit 103 / 5, FAIL and WARN lines identical.
- **`context_map.py --check`:** fresh.
- **Test file:** 241/241, EXAMINED 241, all 20 T079 ids present.
- **Not run:** the `owner_browser_build` render (needs a wasm download); `scan_debt` and `research_dod`, both untouched by the diff.
